name: causal_tracing
label: Causal Tracing
description: Locates where a model recalls the facts it knows, by corrupting the input and restoring one site at a time, and reports how reliably that is in early-to-mid MLP layers. One trace per model and format; no editing method is involved.

field_groups.label: Tracing
field_groups.note: how the causal effect is measured

options.label: GPT-J-6B
options.note: traced in the original ROME paper: the check that this script agrees

options.label: GPT-OSS-20B
options.note: no locate-and-edit hparams yet; mixture-of-experts MLP, so its mlp curve means something slightly different

fields.name: data_path
fields.label: Prompts
fields.note: tracing needs facts the model already knows, so only datasets carrying the true answer (not just an edit target) are listed. Ignored when a fact set is chosen.

subsets.label: wiki_counterfact
subsets.note: ground_truth is the fact the model should already hold

subsets.label: ZsRE
subsets.note: true answer recovered from the 'cond' field

subsets.label: wiki_recent
subsets.note: post-training facts: the model is not expected to know them, so there is no recall to localize

subsets.label: CF-3k-v2
subsets.note: single-fact rewrites with their true answers, ROME-style completions over 37 Wikidata relations

subsets.label: all 25 domains
subsets.note: real Wikidata facts across 25 knowledge domains; trace through a fact set (select_facts.py reads every domain file)

subsets.label: by question type
subsets.note: news questions with four choices (format mcq / chat_mcq); trace through a fact set

subsets.label: altered riddles
subsets.note: riddles with an added clue that changes the answer (format riddle / chat_riddle); the clue is what gets corrupted

fields.name: split
fields.label: Records
fields.note: which records of the dataset to scan. The trace informs edit layers, so it stays off test records like every sweep.

fields.name: fact_set
fields.label: Fact set

options.label: none: scan the dataset per model
MQuAKE, shared by Qwen3-4B base + instruct
MQuAKE, shared by Olmo-3-7B base + instruct
MQuAKE, shared by Llama-3.1-8B base + instruct
MQuAKE, shared by Mistral-7B base + instruct

fields.note: a fixed list from fact selection: every model traces the same facts. The page lists the sets on disk.

fields.name: format
fields.label: Prompt format

options.label: completion
options.note: the cloze sentence; noise on the subject

options.label: question
options.note: 'Question: ... Answer:' as plain text; noise on the subject

options.label: chat_question
options.note: the question through the model's chat template, asking for the answer only; noise on the subject

options.label: chat_prefill
options.note: the question through the chat template, with the cloze sentence begun as the reply; noise on every mention of the subject

options.label: mcq
options.note: question, lettered choices, 'Answer:' as plain text; noise on the question

options.label: chat_mcq
options.note: the multiple-choice prompt through the chat template, asking for the letter only; noise on the question

options.label: riddle
options.note: 'Riddle: ... Answer:' as plain text; noise on the clue the altered riddle added

options.label: chat_riddle
options.note: the riddle through the chat template, asking for the answer only; noise on the added clue

fields.note: how each fact is written; chat_* go through the model's chat template (instruct models)

fields.name: n_prompts
fields.label: Prompts to trace
fields.note: after the known-fact filter. The published traces use ~1000; 200 already gives a stable peak.

fields.name: min_prob
fields.label: Minimum recall probability
fields.note: a fact the model barely recalls has little recall to localize

fields.name: known_check
fields.label: Known-fact check
fields.note: generate: the model answers and must say an accepted answer; what it writes first becomes the lead-in, and the answer is traced where the model gives it. first_token: the answer's first token must be the very next token (the original test)

options.label: the model answers, the answer must appear (generate)
the next token must be the answer (first_token)

fields.name: judge
fields.label: Judge
fields.note: asked only about answers that do not contain an accepted answer: it may accept an equivalent (NYC for New York City). ollama runs a small local model on the job's own GPU; api uses evaluation.local.json

fields.name: judge_model
fields.label: Judge model
fields.note: empty: qwen3:4b-instruct for Ollama, the configured model for the API

fields.name: max_candidates
fields.label: Records to scan
fields.note: upper bound on records read looking for prompts that pass the filter

fields.name: effect
fields.label: Layer chosen from
fields.note: all three curves are always recorded; this picks which one names the layer in traced_layers.json

fields.name: window
fields.label: Restore window
fields.note: layers restored together for the mlp/attn curves (ROME uses 10). Ignored by the hidden-state curve, which restores one layer at a time.

fields.name: sever
fields.label: Severing test
fields.note: restore the hidden state with later MLPs or attention frozen: are the MLPs needed to carry the fact?

fields.name: noise_scale
fields.label: Subject noise
fields.note: in units of this model's embedding standard deviation (ROME uses 3)

fields.name: n_noise_samples
fields.label: Noise samples
fields.note: corrupted runs averaged per measurement; also the batch size of every forward pass

fields.name: token_grid
fields.label: Full token grid
fields.note: trace every token position, not just the last subject token, for this many prompts - the heatmap. Costs roughly one prompt-length multiple per prompt, so keep it small.

fields.name: dtype
fields.label: Precision
fields.note: probabilities are always compared in fp32 regardless; this is the forward pass itself
